{{nihongo|'''Iya Shrine'''|揖夜神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

'''Iya Shrine''' (いやじんじゃ / いふやじんじゃ) is a shrine in Iya, Higashiizumo-chō, {{ill|Matsue|Q207321|qid=Q207321}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is one of the {{ill|Ou district|ja|意宇郡|zh|意宇郡|qid=Q11073594|lt=Oi six shrines}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, it was formerly gōsha and later prefectural shrine. It is near a site identified with {{ill|Yomotsu Hirasaka|Q22084535|qid=Q22084535}} from {{ill|Japanese mythology|ar|أساطير يابانية|ast|Mitoloxía xaponesa|az|Yapon mifologiyası|bjn|Mitologi Japang|ca|Mitologia japonesa|cs|Japonská mytologie|de|Japanische Mythologie|el|Ιαπωνική μυθολογία|eo|Japana mitologio|es|Mitología japonesa|eu|Japoniar mitologia|fa|اسطوره‌شناسی ژاپنی|fi|Japanilainen mytologia|fr|Mythologie japonaise|he|מיתולוגיה יפנית|hi|जापानी पौराणिक कथाओं|hr|Japanska mitologija|hu|Japán mitológia|hy|Ճապոնական դիցաբանություն|ia|Mythologia japonese|id|Mitologi Jepang|it|Mitologia giapponese|ja|日本神話|jv|Mitologi Jepang|ka|იაპონური მითოლოგია|ko|일본 신화|la|Mythologia Iaponiae|lt|Japonų mitologija|min|Mitologi Japang|mk|Јапонска митологија|ms|Mitologi Jepun|my|ဂျပန်ဒဏ္ဍာရီ|nl|Japanse mythologie|no|Japansk mytologi|or|ଜାପାନୀ ଧର୍ମକଥା|pl|Mitologia japońska|pt|Mitologia japonesa|ro|Mitologia japoneză|ru|Японская мифология|sh|Japanska mitologija|simple|Japanese mythology|sk|Japonská mytológia|sr|Japanska mitologija|sv|Japansk mytologi|szy|nu Lipun a micidekay a kungku|tl|Mitolohiyang Hapones|tr|Japon mitolojisi|uk|Японська міфологія|uz|Yapon mifologiyasi|vi|Thần thoại Nhật Bản|zh|日本神話|qid=Q814158|lt=Kiki mythology}}. On nearby Hibayama in neighboring Yasugi there is also a related sacred trace identified as Izanami's tomb in the Kojiki.

=== History ===
It is identified with "Kotoya-sha" in the {{ill|Empress Kōgyoku|ar|الإمبراطورة كوغيوكو|arz|الامبراطوره كوجيوكو|azb|امپراتریس کوقیوکو|bcl|Emperatris Kōgyoku|ca|Kōgyoku|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆگیۆکو|cs|Kógjoku|de|Kōgyoku|es|Kōgyoku|eu|Kōgyoku|fa|امپراتریس کوگیوکو|fi|Kōgyoku|fr|Kōgyoku|hak|Kōgyoku Thiên-fòng|hu|Kógjoku japán császárnő|id|Kōgyoku|it|Kōgyoku|ja|斉明天皇|ka|კოგიოკუ|ko|고교쿠 천황|my|ကိုးကီယိုကုဧကရီ|nl|Kogyoku|pl|Kōgyoku|pt|Kogyoku|ru|Императрица Когёку|sh|Carica Kōgyoku|simple|Empress Kōgyoku|sl|Cesarica Kogjoku|sv|Kogyoku|ta|பேரரசி கோக்யோகு|th|จักรพรรดินีโคเงียวกุ|tl|Emperatris Kōgyoku|tr|Kōgyoku (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Коґьоку|uz|Imperator Kōgyoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōgyoku|wuu|皇极天皇|zh|皇极天皇|zh_classical|皇極天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôgyoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|皇極天皇|qid=Q235296}} year-5 entry of the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' ("A dog bit off a dead person's arm and left it at Kotoya-sha"), with "Ifuya-sha" listed as shrine under Jingikan in the Oi District section of the '{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}},' and with "Iya Shrine" in Oi District, Izumo Province, of the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'.

According to the '{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}', its {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} was raised to Junior Fifth Upper in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 (867), then to Senior Fifth Lower in Jōgan 13.

According to documents preserved at the shrine, in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012}} it was called "Iya Taisha," and from the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}} it was called "Iya Daimyōjin."

From the end of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} to the Nanboku-chō era, the Ōya clan sent as estate officers served as shrine office called "Bekka" and controlled this shrine. From the {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}} onward, by order of the {{ill|Izumo clan|Q11395856|qid=Q11395856}}, the Akigami family priests of {{ill|Kamosu Shrine|Q3192477|qid=Q3192477}} concurrently served as priests. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the Inoue family became Bekka and continue to today. Shizuga, branched from the Inoue family, was a painter using the name Kanaya; his son was master carpenter Kawashima Tokujirō. Even now, construction rites receive offerings from the Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko house.

=== Shrine buildings ===
;Haiden
;Honden: {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|qid=Q387874}}, but interior orientation is opposite that of {{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}}.
;Karakuni Itate Shrine: identified with "Ifuya-sha" (Jingikan-listed) in the Izumo Fudoki and Engishiki "Karakuni Itate Shrine seated in same complex." Deities: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}. Located left of honden.
;Mihotsuhime Shrine: identified with "Ifuya-sha" (not under Jingikan) in the Izumo Fudoki. Deity: {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|Q6378698|qid=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}. Located right of honden.

=== Festivals ===
* Jan 3: Mita-uchi Festival
* May 28: Otaue Festival
* Aug 28: Hokake Festival
* Oct 19: {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}
 etc.
;Hokake Festival: On the preceding day (27th), priests purify at Sodeshi-ga-ura on {{ill|Nakaumi|Q1077275|qid=Q1077275}}, then prepare offerings such as amazake and roasted rice at the shrine office. On festival day, after morning rites, prepared offerings are presented at 75 locations in the precinct. In the afternoon, the mikoshi is loaded on a boat and carried to Hitotsu-ishi about 500 m offshore from Sodeshi-ga-ura, where offerings are made in the "Hitotsu-ishi {{ill|Shinko-shiki|Q123907414|qid=Q123907414}}."

=== Yomotsu Hirasaka ===
A place identified as {{ill|Yomotsu Hirasaka|Q22084535|qid=Q22084535}} (boundary with {{ill|Zbigniew Wilczkiewicz|Q15846115|qid=Q15846115}} / {{ill|Ne-no-kuni|Q7555425|qid=Q7555425}}) appearing in Kiki myths such as {{ill|Kamiumi|Q3545159|qid=Q3545159}} and {{ill|Myth of Ōkuninushi|Q11433656|qid=Q11433656}} lies east of this shrine in Hiraga, Iya-chō, marked by a stone monument<ref>[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/admin/seisaku/koho/esque/2011/81/02.html Yomotsu Hirasaka, passage to the underworld] Shimane Prefecture "Shimanesque" No.81 (2011)</ref>.
=== Ajisukitakahikone and Amenowakahiko ===
The place where {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami}} is said to have toppled and kicked away {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amenowakahiko}}'s mourning hut is said to have been this shrine site.<ref>Manga artist {{ill|Yoshikazu Yasuhiko|Q1049526|qid=Q1049526}} places the presumed site here in his manga "Jinmu."</ref>
